title: What was daily life like before indoor plumbing?
sources: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

lines.text: What was daily life like in American cities just one hundred and fifty years ago before indoor plumbing?
lines.caps: What was life *really like | before indoor *plumbing?

lines.text: It was vastly dirtier and more perilous than anyone realizes.
lines.caps: Vastly *dirtier | and more dangerous than you *think!

lines.text: Every family kept porcelain chamber pots beneath their beds for nighttime calls of nature.
lines.caps: Chamber pots sat *under beds | for midnight *trips

lines.text: In the morning, people dumped the contents into wooden backyard outhouses or straight into city street gutters.
Raw waste seeped into shallow well drinking water, sparking deadly cholera and typhoid fever epidemics.
lines.caps: Waste seeped into *wells | causing deadly *cholera outbreaks

lines.text: Baths were a luxury taken once a week, sharing the same heated kettle water among multiple family members.
lines.caps: Baths were a *weekly luxury | sharing the same tub of *water

lines.text: Indoor plumbing and sanitary sewer networks saved more human lives than almost any medical invention in history.
lines.caps: Modern sewers saved *more lives | than any modern *medicine!
